Hi Morgan — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up front, then a slightly more detailed operational breakdown below. Happy to move any of this into an official attestation/DocuSign.

Short assurance:
- Redwood does not train its production model-training pipelines on identifiable customer content from hosted or dedicated deployments when a customer has opted into our "no-derivative-modeling" configuration. That includes prompts, documents, and uploaded artifacts.

Operational retention nuances (high level):
- Inference telemetry (routing/latency/aggregate counters): retained in a high-throughput tier for 72 hours to support routing and hot-cache heuristics; then aggregated and rolled up into non-identifiable counters for 13 months for billing/analytics.
- KV/prefix caches: ephemeral and tied to active sessions; cache entries are evicted based on LRU and are never materialized into training stores. Typical TTL is minutes — rarely beyond 24 hours except for pinned customer sessions.
- Debug/incident snapshots: when an active incident requires a snapshot, we create an encrypted debugging snapshot that is stored in an ops-only bucket for up to 7 days, with tight KMS controls and an audit log. These snapshots are never ingested into model-training pipelines.
- Backups & cold snapshots: daily encrypted backups are rotated on a customer-separated schedule. Cold backup retention is configurable; default automatic overwrite/rotation occurs on a 90-day cycle for hosted customers.
- Deletion flow: customers can request immediate account/content deletion. We run a three-phase purge: tombstone marker (within 24 hrs), prune from hot/nearline stores (within 72 hrs), and schedule cold backup removal on next rotation (within 90 days). We provide a deletion certificate (GUID + timestamp) when the tombstone and hot-prune complete; final cold-backup pruning certificate follows once rotation completes.

Attachments: I've uploaded a short FAQ and a diagram for the deletion flow: data_retention_FAQ_v2.pdf, erase_flow_diagram.png.

Next steps: I can do a 30-minute call with legal to walk through these items and provide an official signed attestation (DocuSign) if that's required for the PO. Proposed times: tomorrow 10:30–11:00 PT or 15:00–15:30 PT.

Best,

Thanks Naomi — that level of detail helps. A couple follow-ups from legal and engineering:

1) Snapshots vs. backups: are the daily cold backups ever used for offline analysis (e.g., sampling for quality review) outside of restore/recovery? If yes, are those processes explicitly excluded from training?

2) For the "no-derivative-modeling" configuration, is there an audit log that we (or your compliance team) can provide to our security team showing the opt-out flag and a record of requests?

3) If a developer within our tenant created a transient debugging snapshot (e.g., to investigate a customer bug) and then deleted it, what's the practical window where that content could still exist in any system (hot, nearline, cold)? Legal wants a conservative SLA to put in the contract.

We'd like the deletion certificate artifact and a short statement we can attach to the PO. A DocuSign attestation would be ideal. 10:30 PT tomorrow works for me.

—Morgan

Subject: Re: Evidence request: not used for training + retention details

Morgan — great questions. Quick clarifications below and a proposed wording for the attestation.

1) Cold backups: by default backups are retained strictly for restore and disaster recovery. We have a written policy that cold backups are not used for model training or corpus construction. Any exception would require an explicit engineering change and a documented, auditable approval path (not done in normal ops).

2) Audit trail for opt-out: yes — the "no-derivative-modeling" flag is recorded in our control-plane events stream. We can provide an export of the control-plane audit events (timestamped) that shows the opt-out flag, the user who set it, and the tenant ID. That export is available as a CSV or signed PDF on request.

3) Developer/transient snapshots: operationally, the conservative window is: tombstone within 24 hours of a deletion request or snapshot deletion, removal from hot/nearline within 72 hours, and cold-backup rotation within 90 days. We will include that conservative SLA language in the attestation. For additional assurance we can:
- Offer a one-time attestation (DocuSign) that lists FinovateAI tenant ID and the effective opt-out date.
- Provide the deletion certificate (GUID) when hot/nearline prune completes and a follow-up certificate after cold backup rotation.

Proposed attestation wording (short):
"Redwood Inference attests that, for FinovateAI (tenant ID: FIN-8421) while the 'no-derivative-modeling' configuration is active: (1) identifiable customer content will not be used to train or fine-tune Redwood's model training pipelines; (2) the deletion workflow will tombstone content within 24 hours, prune hot/nearline systems within 72 hours, and schedule cold-backup removal on the next 90-day rotation; (3) control-plane audit events reflecting the opt-out flag will be provided upon request. A deletion certificate will be issued when the hot/nearline prune completes, with final confirmation after cold-backup rotation."

If that language looks good I will issue the DocuSign and attach the two artifacts we discussed: the audit export template and a deletion-flow diagram. Shall I proceed? If so, please confirm the tenant ID we should include in the attestation (you can reply with it privately if you prefer).

Thanks — look forward to the call tomorrow 10:30 PT.

—Naomi
